q: 设计 Google Docs 时，以下哪些属于核心功能需求（in scope）？（多选）
q_en: When designing Google Docs, which items are core in-scope functional requirements?
options: 多个用户并发编辑同一文档
实时看到其他协作者的修改
文档权限与协作级别管理
看到其他用户的光标位置与在场状态
why: 核心需求是：创建文档、多人并发编辑、实时看到彼此修改、光标/在场。权限、版本历史、复杂文档结构都被明确划到 out of scope。
why_en: The core requirements are creating documents, concurrent editing, seeing each other's changes in real time, and cursor presence, while permissions and versioning are out of scope.
options_en: Multiple users editing the same document concurrently
Seeing collaborators' changes in real time
Managing document permissions and collaboration levels
Seeing other users' cursor positions and presence
optionExplanations: 多人同时改同一份文档是协同编辑的定义，系统必须处理并发写入，这是范围内的核心能力。
光有并发编辑还不够，还要让每个人几乎实时看到别人的改动，这条决定了要上低延迟推送通道。
权限模型（谁能读/写/评论）没被列进这道题要做的功能，设计先只管协同编辑本身。
光标位置和在场状态让协作者知道谁在、在哪编辑，是 awareness 体验的数据基础。
optionExplanations_en: Multiple people editing the same document at once is the definition of collaborative editing, so the system has to handle concurrent writes as a core requirement.
Seeing each other's changes almost immediately is what makes editing feel collaborative, and it's why the design needs a low-latency push channel.
Access-control roles never made it onto this design's feature list, so it stays focused purely on the editing mechanics.
Cursor position and presence tell collaborators who's in the document and where, which is the data behind the awareness feature.

q: 以下哪一项被明确划为 out of scope（不做）？
q_en: Which item is explicitly out of scope for this Google Docs design?
options: 多人同时编辑一份文档
文档历史与版本回退
实时同步彼此的修改
显示协作者光标
why: 版本历史、权限管理、富文本复杂结构都不在范围内——假设一个简单的纯文本编辑器，聚焦协同编辑本身。
why_en: Document history and versioning, permissions, and rich document structure are explicitly out of scope so the design can focus on collaboration itself.
options_en: Multiple people editing one document at once
Document history and version rollback
Real-time syncing of everyone's changes
Showing collaborators' cursors
optionExplanations: 并发编辑本身是核心功能，不是被排除的一项。
版本历史和回退需要额外存储和界面支持，这道题把它明确划出范围，先聚焦协同编辑本身。
实时同步彼此的修改正是这个产品的核心承诺，同样在范围内。
显示协作者光标是 awareness 体验的一部分，也在范围内。
optionExplanations_en: Concurrent editing is a core in-scope feature, not the excluded one.
Version history and rollback need extra storage and UI, and this design explicitly puts them out of scope to stay focused on collaboration itself.
Real-time syncing of edits is the product's core promise, so it stays in scope.
Showing collaborator cursors is part of the awareness experience, also in scope.

scenario: 设计一个 Google Docs 类协同编辑器：用户要实时看到编辑结果，单文档协作者有限，但全站用户和文档数量很大。
scenario_en: You are designing a Google Docs-style collaborative editor where edits must feel real time, one document has bounded collaborators, and the whole service has many users and documents.
q: 这些非功能数字各自约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Complete the non-functional constraints and the design consequence for Google Docs.
text: 更新延迟低于 {{100ms}}，所以编辑通道要用低延迟长连接；单文档最多 {{100}} 个编辑者，所以中心式 OT 可行；数{{百万}}并发用户要求 WebSocket 水平扩展；数十{{亿}}文档要求操作日志压实。
why: 这些是给定目标，不是推导结果；它们分别约束实时通道、并发编辑算法、连接层扩展和存储压实。数字的用途是把后面的架构选择收窄。
why_en: These are input constraints, not facts to memorize: they drive the real-time channel, the OT choice, WebSocket scaling, and log compaction.

q: Google Docs 类协同文档编辑器的规模目标（非功能需求）是？
q_en: What scale target should this Google Docs-style collaborative editor support?
options: 数千用户、数百万文档
数百万并发用户、数百万文档
数百万并发用户、数十亿文档
数十亿并发用户、数十亿文档
why: 目标是数百万并发用户、数十亿文档；但单文档编辑者被限制在 100 以内，所以单文档吞吐并不恐怖，难点在连接数和存储量。
why_en: The system targets millions of concurrent users across billions of documents, while each single document stays small thanks to the editor cap.
options_en: Thousands of users, millions of documents
Millions of concurrent users, millions of documents
Millions of concurrent users, billions of documents
Billions of concurrent users, billions of documents
optionExplanations: 数千用户、数百万文档低估了产品级流量，会让容量设计偏小。
并发用户量级对，但文档规模被低估——十亿级文档意味着存储和压实要另算一笔账。
百万级并发用户、十亿级文档是这道题给定的量级锚点，后续连接数和存储设计都围绕它展开。
十亿级并发用户超出了协同文档产品的现实规模，把目标定得过大。
optionExplanations_en: Thousands of users and millions of documents undershoots the real product scale and would size capacity too small.
The user count is right, but billions of documents is the harder number — it drives storage and compaction planning, not just connections.
Millions of concurrent users and billions of documents is the scale anchor this design works from for connection count and storage sizing.
Billions of concurrent users overshoots what a collaborative document product realistically needs to support.

q: 「单文档最多 100 个并发编辑者」这条约束给设计带来什么好处？
q_en: What design benefit comes from capping one document at 100 concurrent editors?
options: 反正编辑者少，可以完全不做持久化处理
反正编辑者少，可以放弃低延迟实时性要求
反正编辑者少，可以选择最终一致以外的模型
单文档写吞吐有上限，让中心式 OT 服务器变得可行
why: 限制编辑者数量意味着单文档流量有上限，可以放心用「一台服务器独占一个文档」的 OT 架构。真实的 Google Docs 也这么做：超过上限后新用户只能以读者身份加入。
why_en: Capping concurrent editors bounds per-document throughput, which is exactly what makes a central OT server per document feasible, and real Google Docs does the same by demoting overflow users to readers.
options_en: Editors are few, so persistence can be skipped entirely
Editors are few, so the low-latency real-time requirement can be dropped
Editors are few, so a model other than eventual consistency can be used
Per-document write throughput stays bounded, making a central OT server feasible

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 编辑者数量不影响持久性要求，重启后文档仍要可恢复，这个好处不成立。
编辑者少不代表可以牺牲响应速度，实时手感是协同编辑的核心承诺，跟人数无关。
一致性模型的选择取决于「协同天然会短暂分歧」，跟编辑者数量没有因果关系。
把编辑者数量摁住，就等于把单文档写吞吐摁住，中心式 OT 服务器才扛得住这份责任。
optionExplanations_en: A smaller editor count doesn't relax durability — documents still need to survive a restart, so this benefit doesn't hold.
Fewer editors doesn't excuse dropping responsiveness; the real-time feel is core to collaborative editing regardless of headcount.
The consistency model follows from collaboration naturally diverging briefly, not from how many editors there are.
Pinning down the editor count pins down per-document write throughput, which is what makes a central OT server able to carry that load.

q: Google Docs 类协同文档编辑器对文档内容选择的一致性模型是？
q_en: What consistency model should the document content use in a Google Docs-style editor?
options: 最终一致：所有用户最终看到相同的文档状态
强一致：每次编辑全员立即同步可见
读己之写一致
因果一致且不允许任何乱序
why: 协同编辑天然会有短暂分歧（各自本地先应用），要求的是收敛：不管操作以什么顺序到达，所有副本最终一致。
why_en: The document is eventually consistent, meaning replicas may briefly diverge but every user converges on the same final state.
options_en: Eventual consistency: all users eventually see the same document state
Strong consistency: every edit is visible to everyone instantly
Read-your-writes consistency
Causal consistency with no reordering allowed
optionExplanations: 协同编辑允许短暂分歧，只要最终所有副本收敛到同一文档，这正是这里要的一致性承诺。
强一致要求每次编辑立刻全员可见，代价是要阻塞写入，百万并发根本扛不住。
读己之写只保证自己看到自己的改动，不保证收敛到统一状态，不是协作要的收敛保证。
因果一致要求严格保序，对文本编辑来说保证过强也没必要，OT/CRDT 只需要收敛。
optionExplanations_en: Collaborative editing tolerates brief divergence as long as every replica converges on the same final document, which is exactly the guarantee needed here.
Strong consistency would make every edit visible everywhere instantly, which means blocking writes — not survivable at millions of concurrent users.
Read-your-writes only guarantees you see your own edit, not that everyone converges on one state, so it misses the point of collaboration.
Causal consistency demands strict ordering, which is stronger than text editing needs — OT and CRDT only require eventual convergence.

q: 「服务器重启后文档仍然可用」这条持久性需求，对写路径的直接约束是？
q_en: If documents must survive a server restart, what does that require on the write path?
options: 所有文档必须常驻内存，重启就会丢失编辑
编辑必须全部走客户端本地存储，服务器不落盘
编辑写入持久化存储成功后才向用户确认
必须使用强一致关系数据库才能持久化
why: 持久性意味着操作不能只留在服务器内存里：先落库（操作日志），成功后再 ack 给用户，重启后可从库中重放恢复。
why_en: Durability means an edit is acknowledged only after it is recorded in persistent storage, so a server restart can replay the log instead of losing work.
options_en: All documents must stay resident in memory — a restart loses every edit
Every edit must go through client-side local storage, with nothing written on the server
An edit is acknowledged to the user only after it is durably written to storage
A strongly consistent relational database is required for durability
optionExplanations: 把文档全放内存等于放弃持久化承诺，进程一重启编辑就没了。
只写客户端本地存储，别的协作者和服务器都看不到这份编辑，协作根本无从谈起。
落库成功再确认，是这条约束下唯一能保证重启后可恢复的做法。
持久性只要求「写下来能恢复」，不等于必须上强一致关系数据库，日志型存储也能满足。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping every document only in memory abandons durability outright — a restart wipes every edit.
Client-only local storage never reaches the server or other collaborators, so it can't support real collaboration at all.
Acknowledging only after a durable write is the one approach here that guarantees recovery after a restart.
Durability just means the write can be replayed on recovery; it doesn't force a strongly consistent relational database — an append-only log works too.

q: 以下哪些是这个设计的核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which entities are core to this collaborative document design?
options: Document（文档）
Cursor（光标/在场）
Permission（权限）
Edit（编辑操作）
why: 四个核心实体：Editor（编辑者）、Document（文档）、Edit（一次修改）、Cursor（光标位置与在场）。权限被划出范围，不是实体。
why_en: The core entities are the editor, the document, the edit, and the cursor with presence, while permissions are out of scope.
options_en: Document
Cursor (position and presence)
Permission
Edit (a change operation)
optionExplanations: 文档承载内容、元数据和版本指针，是所有其他实体挂靠的中心对象。
光标把位置和在场状态绑在一起，是 awareness 功能追踪和广播的数据源。
权限被划出范围，管访问不属于这道题要建模的实体。
一次编辑操作是协同流的基本单位，OT/CRDT 都围绕它运转。
optionExplanations_en: The document carries content, metadata, and a version pointer — the central object every other entity attaches to.
The cursor bundles position and presence together, feeding the data that awareness tracking and broadcast rely on.
Permissions are out of scope here, so access control isn't one of the entities this design models.
A single edit operation is the basic unit of the collaboration stream, and both OT and CRDT operate on it.

q: Cursor 这个实体承载的是什么信息？
q_en: What information does the Cursor entity carry?
options: 文档内容的最新完整快照，跟光标无关
光标位置和在场状态（presence）
这次编辑操作生成时的时间戳记录
该用户在系统里的权限访问级别
why: Cursor 既是位置也是在场信号：它告诉其他协作者「谁在这份文档里、正在哪儿编辑」，是 awareness 功能的数据基础。
why_en: The cursor entity captures both where an editor's caret sits and that user's live presence in the document.
options_en: The latest full snapshot of the document content, unrelated to the cursor
Cursor position plus presence state
The timestamp recorded when this edit operation was generated
This user's permission and access level in the system
optionExplanations: 完整内容快照是文档实体的信息，不是 Cursor 要携带的东西。
Cursor 把「光标在哪」和「这个人还在不在线」绑在一起，正是 awareness 需要的两件事。
时间戳是操作日志的属性，用来定序，不属于 Cursor 实体。
权限级别归 Permission 管，这道题已经把权限划出范围。
optionExplanations_en: A full content snapshot belongs to the Document entity, not to Cursor.
Cursor ties together where the caret sits and whether that person is still online — exactly the two things awareness needs.
A timestamp belongs to the operation log for ordering, not to the Cursor entity.
Permission level is the Permission entity's job, and permissions are out of scope for this design anyway.

scenario: 编辑过程中客户端要高频发送小操作（插入/删除/移动光标），服务器也要随时把别人的操作推回来，往返延迟要求 < 100ms。
scenario_en: During editing, clients send frequent small operations like inserts, deletes, and cursor moves, while the server must push other users' operations back with under 100 ms round-trip latency.
q: 编辑通道最合适的通信方式是？
q_en: What communication method best fits the editing channel?
options: 客户端每秒轮询 REST 接口
WebSocket 双向长连接
每次编辑发一个独立 HTTP POST
SSE 单向推送
why: 协同编辑是典型的高频双向场景：客户端持续发操作，服务器持续推别人的操作，WebSocket 的双向长连接正好匹配。
why_en: Collaborative editing needs high-frequency bidirectional messages under one hundred milliseconds, which is exactly what a persistent WebSocket connection provides.
whenOtherWins: 低频的请求-响应操作（创建文档、改标题这类元数据管理）用普通 REST 更简单；只需服务器单向推送时 SSE 也够。
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Editor client] <--> WS[WebSocket server]
    WS --> Collab[Collaboration service]
    Collab --> Log[(Operation log)]
    Collab --> Peers[Other editors]
tradeoff: WebSocket 双向长连接 vs REST 轮询/单向推送
options_en: Client polls a REST endpoint once a second
A bidirectional WebSocket connection
Send each edit as its own HTTP POST
One-way SSE push from server to client

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器单向持续推送更新给客户端的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, or Server-Sent Events, lets a server continuously push updates to a client in one direction only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于标准 HTTP 方法的请求-响应风格接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a request-response API style built on standard HTTP methods.

optionExplanations: REST 轮询每秒才问一次，延迟和无谓请求都撑不住 <100ms 的编辑体验，更适合创建文档这类低频操作。
WebSocket 只用一次握手就能维持一条双向管道，插入、删除、光标移动都能挤在同一条连接上来回跑，天然贴合编辑器的收发节奏。
每次编辑单开一个 HTTP POST，连接建立开销比编辑本身还贵，量一大就先被压垮。
SSE 只能服务器往客户端推，没有上行通道，客户端发操作还是得另开一条路，适合纯只读的更新流。
optionExplanations_en: Polling REST once a second adds real latency and wasted requests, so it fits low-frequency operations like creating a document, not sub-100ms editing.

WebSocket needs one handshake to hold open a two-way pipe, so inserts, deletes, and cursor moves can all ride the same connection in both directions — a natural fit for the editor's send-and-receive rhythm.
Opening a fresh HTTP POST per edit pays connection overhead bigger than the edit itself, and collapses under real typing volume.
SSE only pushes server to client with no upstream channel, so edits would still need a separate path — it fits a read-only update stream instead.

q: 读这份 WebSocket 协议草案：客户端发送（SEND）和接收（RECV）的消息类型分别是？
q_en: In this WebSocket protocol draft, which message types does the client send and receive?
options: SEND: update；RECV: insert/delete/updateCursor
SEND 和 RECV 都是 update
SEND: insert/delete/updateCursor；RECV: update
全部通过 REST 端点完成
why: 客户端把自己的 insert/delete/updateCursor 发上去，服务器把别人已确认的操作打包成 update 推回来；文档创建这类管理操作仍走 REST。
why_en: Clients send insert, delete, and cursor updates over the socket while the server pushes back update messages, with document creation staying on a REST endpoint.
options_en: SEND carries update; RECV carries insert, delete, and updateCursor
Both SEND and RECV use a generic update message
SEND carries insert, delete, and updateCursor; RECV carries update
Everything happens through REST endpoints

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于标准 HTTP 方法的请求-响应风格接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a request-response API style built on standard HTTP methods.

optionExplanations: 方向反了：草案里是客户端 SEND 三类编辑消息，服务器 RECV 后再广播 update，不是反过来。
把 SEND/RECV 都写成通用 update 抹掉了协议里客户端发意图、服务器发结果这个区分。
SEND 走三类编辑意图，RECV 只回一种确认结果，这个不对称正是草案要表达的协议分工。
文档创建走 REST 没错，但编辑操作本身走的是这条 WebSocket，不是全部走 REST。
optionExplanations_en: The direction is backwards: the client SENDs the three edit types and the server RECVs then broadcasts update, not the other way around.
Collapsing both SEND and RECV into a generic update message erases the distinction between client intent and server-confirmed result.
SEND carries three kinds of edit intent while RECV only ever answers with one confirmation type — that asymmetry is exactly the protocol split the draft defines.
Document creation does use REST, but the edit messages themselves ride this WebSocket, not REST end to end.

q: API 设计里引入 WebSocket 后，表达方式上要注意什么？
q_en: When adding WebSocket to the API design, what should the API description focus on?
options: 把每条消息单独定义成一个 HTTP 端点
WebSocket 连接不需要定义任何协议
描述连接上收发的消息 schema，而非 HTTP 端点
必须使用 protobuf 编码才算合格
why: WebSocket 是一条长连接，API 设计要描述连接上流动的消息类型和结构；具体记法随意，但要能讲清楚线上传的是什么。
why_en: With websockets you describe the messages flowing over the connection rather than HTTP endpoints, and any clear notation for the message schema works.
options_en: Define every message as its own HTTP endpoint
WebSocket needs no protocol definition at all
Describe the message schema flowing over the connection, not HTTP endpoints
You must use protobuf encoding to be valid

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向长连接，适合高频双向通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server, well suited to high-frequency two-way messaging.

optionExplanations: 把每条消息拆成独立 HTTP 端点，等于用请求-响应的框架硬套一条持续连接，只会制造冗余定义。
完全不定义协议会让客户端和服务器各自猜消息格式，协作起来全靠运气。
描述连接上流动的消息 schema——每种消息长什么样、谁发谁收——才是 WebSocket 该写的 API 文档。
protobuf 只是众多编码之一，JSON 或其他清晰记法同样能把消息说明白，不是强制项。
optionExplanations_en: Treating every message as its own HTTP endpoint forces a request-response frame onto a persistent connection and just creates redundant definitions.
Leaving the protocol fully undefined leaves client and server guessing at message shapes, which breaks interoperability.
Describing the message schema flowing over the connection — what each message looks like and who sends and receives it — is what a WebSocket API doc should cover.
Protobuf is just one encoding option; JSON or any clear notation communicates the schema fine, so it isn't mandatory.

scenario: 存文档元数据（标题、docId，将来可能挂权限、标签），需要灵活查询，初期规模不大、以后可以再分区复制。
scenario_en: Document metadata such as title and docId needs flexible queries; the initial scale is modest, and partitioning or replication can be added later.
q: 元数据库的合理默认选型是？
q_en: What is the sensible default database for document metadata?
options: Cassandra
S3 对象存储
Postgres
本地文件系统
why: 元数据是典型的关系型小数据：Postgres 给灵活查询，规模上来再分区/复制即可，不必一开始过度设计。
why_en: Postgres is the sensible default for document metadata because it offers flexible querying and can be partitioned and replicated later if scale demands.
whenOtherWins: 如果是操作日志这种高频 append-only 写、按文档分区顺序读的负载，Cassandra 这类写优化的宽列存储更合适。
tradeoff: 灵活关系查询 vs 高频 append 写入扩展
options_en: Cassandra
S3 object storage
Postgres
Local filesystem

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化的宽列分布式数据库，常用于高频 append-only 的日志类负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a write-optimized wide-column distributed database, often used for high-frequency append-only log workloads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云对象存储服务，适合存放大文件而非高频小写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is a cloud object storage service suited to large files rather than frequent small writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库，支持灵活查询，适合结构化元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a relational database with flexible querying, well suited to structured metadata.

optionExplanations: Cassandra 为高频 append-only 写优化，元数据这种低频、需要灵活关系查询的负载，换成它反而没有索引和 JOIN 的方便。
S3 是对象存储，适合大文件整存整取，标题、docId 这类结构化小字段用它查询很别扭。
Postgres 给灵活的关系查询和索引，初期规模不大时单机就够，未来需要再加分区或复制。
本地文件系统没有网络访问、没有并发控制，扛不住多实例服务共享同一份元数据。
optionExplanations_en: Cassandra is optimized for high-frequency append-only writes; metadata's low-frequency, flexible relational queries lose the indexes and joins that make it comfortable.
S3 is object storage built for whole large files, and it's awkward for querying small structured fields like title or docId.
Postgres gives flexible relational queries and indexing; a single node handles the early scale fine, with partitioning or replication to add later.
A local filesystem has no network access or concurrency control, so it can't support multiple service instances sharing the same metadata.

q: 为什么把「文档内容」和「文档元数据」分开存储是合理的？
q_en: Why does it make sense to store document content separately from document metadata?
options: 元数据低频结构化，内容是高频操作流，访问模式不同
元数据的数据量比内容大得多
内容必须只能存在关系型数据库里
这样拆分可以省掉 API gateway
why: 元数据是低频读写、结构化、适合关系查询；内容是高频操作流。访问模式不同就该分开，各选各的存储。
why_en: Metadata like permissions, tags, and titles has a completely different access pattern from the high-frequency edit stream, so separating the two lets each use the right store.
options_en: Metadata is low-frequency and structured; content is a high-frequency operation stream — different access patterns
Metadata is simply much larger than content
Content must live only in a relational database
Splitting them just saves an API gateway
optionExplanations: 元数据低频、结构化，适合关系查询；内容是高频操作流，两种访问模式根本不同，分开存才能各选各的引擎。
实际上文档内容的操作日志往往比元数据大得多，规模大小不是分开存储的理由。
把一切都塞进关系数据库是过强的假设，存储选型应该跟着访问模式走，不是跟着数据类型走。
分不分开存数据跟 API gateway 需不需要没有关系，两者是独立的设计决定。
optionExplanations_en: Metadata is low-frequency and structured, well suited to relational queries, while content is a high-frequency operation stream — the access patterns are different enough that each deserves its own store.
In practice the content operation log is often larger than metadata, so size isn't the reason to split them.
Forcing everything into a relational database is too strong an assumption; storage choice should follow the access pattern, not the data type.
Whether to separate the stores has nothing to do with needing an API gateway — they're independent design decisions.

q: 「创建文档」这条路径的架构模式，以及面试里该怎么对待它？
q_en: How should you model the create-document path, and how much interview time should it get?
options: 单机服务架构，值得重点深挖
CRUD+API gateway 套路化，快速带过
必须使用 serverless 才能满足要求
让客户端直接写入数据库
why: API gateway 后面挂一排无状态 CRUD 服务是最常见的模式，面试里应该几句话画完，把时间留给协同编辑这些真正的难点。
why_en: Document creation is a standard horizontally scaled CRUD service behind an API gateway, a pattern you should sketch quickly to save time for the hard parts.
options_en: A single-server setup worth deep exploration
Horizontally scaled CRUD service behind an API gateway — standard, move fast
Serverless is required to meet the requirements
Let clients write to the database directly
optionExplanations: 单机跑全部逻辑是单点故障，也没有任何值得深挖的权衡，面试里花时间讲它性价比很低。
这套路谁都见过，画完就该收手，别在这上面浪费面试官的耐心。
Serverless 有冷启动和连接管理的额外成本，对这个场景不是必须项，属于过度工程。
让客户端直接写数据库跳过了校验和一致性把关，安全和数据完整性都没法保证。
optionExplanations_en: A single server running everything is a single point of failure with no interesting tradeoff worth exploring, so it's a poor use of interview time.
Everyone has seen this pattern before — sketch it and move on, rather than spending the interviewer's patience here.
Serverless adds cold-start and connection overhead that this path doesn't need — over-engineering for a simple CRUD flow.
Letting the client write the database directly skips validation and consistency checks, so neither security nor data integrity is guaranteed.

q: 「每次编辑都把整份文档发给服务器」这个方案，带宽代价大约是什么量级？
q_en: If every edit sends the whole document to the server, what bandwidth cost are we talking about?
options: 每次键入大约传几个字节，量级明显偏小
每次键入大约传几 KB，量级依然偏小
打字快时每次键入要传几百 KB
编辑时不传，只有点保存才传输一次
why: 整篇快照意味着每敲一个键就传整份文档，对一篇普通文档就是几百 KB 一次键入——带宽被彻底浪费。
why_en: Sending the whole document per edit can mean hundreds of kilobytes for every single keystroke, which is wildly inefficient.
scenario: 协同编辑器最初的写路径设计：用户每按一次键，就把整份文档发送给服务器保存。
scenario_en: The first write-path idea is that every keystroke sends the entire document back to the server for saving.
options_en: Roughly a few bytes go out per keystroke, clearly too small a number
Roughly a few kilobytes go out per keystroke, still too small
A fast typist sends hundreds of kilobytes with every keystroke
Nothing is sent while typing — only one transfer happens on save
optionExplanations: 几个字节的量级只对应单字符编辑，远不是整篇 HTML/富文本快照的体积。
几 KB 顶多是一小段文字，一份正常长度的文档远超这个体积。
一份文档常有几百 KB，naive 快照方案下每敲一个键就整份重传，这正是带宽被浪费的量级。
只有保存时才传是另一套设计（本地缓冲、定期同步），不是这里在考的「每次键入都发」方案。
optionExplanations_en: A few bytes only fits a single character, nowhere near the size of a whole document snapshot.
A few kilobytes covers a short passage at most; a normal document is much bigger than that.
A typical document runs hundreds of kilobytes, so a naive full-snapshot design retransmits that much on every single keystroke — the actual scale of the waste.
Only transmitting on save describes a different design (local buffering, periodic sync), not the send-every-keystroke scheme this question is about.

q: 文档为 "Hello!"，A 提交整篇快照 "Hello, world!"，B 同时提交整篇快照 "Hello"。快照覆盖方案的结局是？
q_en: With two concurrent full-document snapshots, what happens under a snapshot-overwrite design?
options: 最后到达的快照直接覆盖一切，另一个人的并发编辑完全丢失
服务器自动合并成 "Hello, world"
两个快照都被拒绝
系统抛出冲突让用户手动解决
why: 整篇覆盖是 last-writer-wins：最终文档完全取决于谁的请求后到，另一个人的修改被无声抹掉，协同体验彻底崩坏。
why_en: With whole-document snapshots the last write wins, so whichever snapshot arrives last silently erases the other user's concurrent edit.
options_en: The last snapshot to arrive silently overwrites everything, losing the other user's edit
The server automatically merges them into "Hello, world"
Both snapshots are rejected
The system raises a conflict for the user to resolve manually
optionExplanations: 整篇覆盖没有合并逻辑，谁的请求后到就整份生效，先到的人的修改被无声吞掉。
整篇快照本身不携带语义信息，服务器没有能力自动合并出 "Hello, world"，这需要单独的合并算法。
拒绝两个快照会让编辑完全卡住，用户体验上不可接受。
抛冲突给用户需要先侦测到冲突，而整篇覆盖方案根本不做检测，用户永远不知道发生了什么。
optionExplanations_en: Whole-document overwrite has no merge logic, so whichever snapshot lands last simply becomes the document, silently erasing the earlier concurrent edit.
A raw snapshot carries no semantic information, so the server has no way to auto-merge into "Hello, world" — that needs a separate merge algorithm.
Rejecting both snapshots blocks editing entirely, which is not an acceptable user experience.
Raising a conflict requires detecting one first, and whole-document overwrite never checks for conflicts, so the user never even finds out.

q: 改为只传编辑操作（如 INSERT(5, ", world") 和 DELETE(6)）后，带宽解决了，但新问题是？
q_en: After switching to sending edit operations only, what new problem remains?
options: 操作数据包太小，网络协议头开销过大
位置基于旧文档状态，INSERT 先到删错字符
服务器缺少持久化机制，无法存储操作
客户端缺少权限，无法生成编辑操作
why: 每个操作的位置隐含了「当时的文档状态」这个上下文；别人的操作先落地后，原始位置就指错了地方。这正是 OT/CRDT 要解决的问题。
why_en: Each edit's position assumes a specific document state, so if another insert lands first, a raw delete at position six removes the wrong character.
diagram:
graph TD
    OpA[Insert at position] --> Context[Depends on version]
    OpB[Delete at position] --> Context
    Context --> Conflict[Concurrent positions shift]
    Conflict --> Transform[OT or CRDT needed]
options_en: The operation packets are too small; protocol header overhead dominates
Positions assume the old state, so an earlier INSERT deletes the wrong character
The server lacks persistence and cannot store operations
The client lacks permission to generate operations

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 操作本身很小，协议头开销不是问题——真正的坑在位置语义，不在包大小。
位置是相对某个文档状态算出来的坐标，中间只要插了别人一手，这个坐标立刻作废——这正是接下来要引入 OT/CRDT 的理由。
持久化机制负责把操作存下来，跟位置语义对不对是两回事，操作照样能落库。
客户端本来就有权限生成编辑操作，限制不在这里。
optionExplanations_en: The operations themselves are small; protocol overhead isn't the real issue — the trap is in position semantics, not packet size.
A position is a coordinate computed against one particular document state, and the moment someone else's edit lands first, that coordinate goes stale — exactly why OT and CRDT enter the picture next.
Persistence just means storing the operation; whether its position is still correct is a separate question, and storage works regardless.
The client already has permission to generate edit operations, so that's not where the limitation is.

q: 解决「编辑操作依赖文档状态上下文」这一根本问题，业界的两大方案家族是？
q_en: What are the two main industry families for handling edit operations that depend on document state?
options: 分布式锁 与 乐观并发控制
两阶段提交 与 Saga
OT 与 CRDT 两大方案家族
版本向量 与 Paxos
why: 两条路：OT 在应用前按先到的操作「变换」后到的操作；CRDT 让操作本身可交换，任意顺序应用都收敛。
why_en: The two families are operational transformation, which rewrites each edit against those before it, and CRDTs, which make every edit commutative.
options_en: Distributed locking and optimistic concurrency control
Two-phase commit and Saga
OT (operational transformation) and CRDT
Version vectors and Paxos

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 分布式锁和乐观并发控制是数据库隔离手段，不是给协同编辑设计的方案家族。
两阶段提交和 Saga 解决的是跨服务事务一致性，跟并发文本编辑不是一回事。
OT 靠中心定序变换操作，CRDT 靠操作可交换收敛，这正是业界解决「操作依赖文档状态」问题的两条路。
版本向量和 Paxos 是分布式系统里的定序/共识工具，不是专门解决文本并发编辑收敛的方案。
optionExplanations_en: Distributed locking and optimistic concurrency are database isolation techniques, not a family built for collaborative text editing.
Two-phase commit and Saga solve cross-service transactional consistency, which is a different problem from concurrent text editing.
OT reorders and transforms operations through a central server while CRDT makes operations commutative — these are the two real industry families for state-dependent edits.
Version vectors and Paxos are ordering and consensus tools for distributed systems in general, not solutions purpose-built for converging concurrent text edits.

q: 读这个 OT 例子：文档 "Hello!"，A 的插入先被应用。B 的 DELETE(6) 必须被变换成什么才能删对感叹号？
q_en: In this OT example, what must B's DELETE(6) transform into to delete the exclamation mark?
codeSample:
# 初始文档: "Hello!"（感叹号在位置 6）
op_a = INSERT(5, ", world")   # 先到并应用 -> "Hello, world!"
op_b = DELETE(6)              # B 基于旧文档生成，本想删 "!"

# transform(op_b, op_a) = ?
options: DELETE(6)，无需变换
DELETE(7)，顺移 1 位
DELETE(12)，顺移 6 位
DELETE(13)，顺移 7 位
why: ", world" 有 7 个字符，插入点在删除目标之前，所以删除位置要 6+7=13，才能删到已经被顺移的感叹号。
why_en: The seven-character insert lands before the delete target, so the delete position shifts from six to thirteen to still hit the exclamation mark.
options_en: DELETE(6), no transform needed
DELETE(7), a one-position shift
DELETE(12), a six-position shift
DELETE(13), a seven-position shift

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 位置完全不变会让删除还停在旧坐标 6，那里现在是插入内容里的逗号，删错了字符。
只顺移 1 位远远不够抵消 7 个字符的插入，还是会删到错误位置。
顺移 6 位比实际插入的 7 个字符少 1，还是差一位，删的仍不是感叹号。
插入发生在删除目标前面，插入了多少字符，删除坐标就要跟着往后挪多少——这里挪 7 位，6 变 13，刚好落在感叹号上。
optionExplanations_en: Leaving the position unchanged still deletes at the old coordinate six, which is now the comma inside the inserted text — the wrong character.
Shifting by only one is nowhere near enough to offset a seven-character insert, so it still deletes the wrong spot.
Shifting by six is one short of the actual seven-character insert, still landing one position off from the exclamation mark.
The insert lands before the delete target, so the delete coordinate has to shift by however many characters were inserted — seven here, taking six to thirteen, landing right on the exclamation mark.

q: OT（操作变换）的工作机制是？
q_en: How does OT, or operational transformation, work?
options: 各客户端各自决定顺序，最后投票裁定
遇到冲突就把操作全部丢弃
给每个字符单独加分布式锁
中心服务器定最终顺序，按已到操作变换后续操作
why: OT 的核心是中心定序 + 变换：服务器收集所有编辑，按已应用的操作重写后到的操作，让它们在新状态下仍表达原意。
why_en: OT funnels all edits through one server that fixes a final order and transforms each incoming operation against those already applied before applying or rebroadcasting it.
options_en: Each client decides its own order, then a vote settles it
Conflicting operations are simply discarded
Every character gets its own distributed lock
A central server fixes the final order and transforms each operation against those already applied

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 各客户端各自定序再投票，等结果出来编辑早就分岔了，收敛不了。
冲突就丢弃操作意味着用户的编辑说没就没，协作产品不能这样对待用户输入。
给每个字符单独加锁在高频编辑下是性能灾难，锁的粒度和数量都不现实。
全部操作先经过一台服务器排好队，再逐个变换成能接在已应用操作后面的形式，这就是 OT 定序加变换的两步走。
optionExplanations_en: Each client deciding its own order and voting afterward means edits have already diverged by the time a result exists — nothing converges.
Discarding conflicting operations means a user's edit can just vanish, which no collaborative product can do to real input.
Locking every individual character is a performance disaster at editing frequency — the lock count and granularity aren't realistic.
Every operation first queues through one server, then gets transformed to fit cleanly after whatever's already applied — ordering plus transformation, the two-step core of OT.

q: OT 最大的架构性代价是什么，本设计靠什么兜住它？
q_en: What is OT's biggest architectural cost, and what constraint contains it here?
options: 内存占用巨大，需要靠压缩机制解决
中心服务器定全序限制协作者规模；靠编辑者上限兜住
无法支持删除操作，需要靠墓碑机制解决
延迟太高，需要靠 CDN 加速解决
why: OT 需要一台服务器给出最终顺序，这限制了协作者数量、而且正确实现很精细；正好非功能需求把编辑者限制在 100 人以内，中心式方案完全够用。
why_en: OT's cost is a required central ordering server that caps collaborator scale and is tricky to implement correctly, which the hundred-editor limit conveniently absorbs.
options_en: Memory use is huge; compression solves it
A central server must fix total order, capping collaborators and inviting bugs; the hundred-editor limit absorbs it
Deletes are unsupported; tombstones solve it
Latency is too high; a CDN solves it

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作变换（Operational Transformation）：用中心服务器给操作定序，并按已应用的操作重写后到操作，使并发编辑收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OT, or operational transformation, uses a central server to order operations and rewrite incoming ones against those already applied so concurrent edits converge.

optionExplanations: 内存占用不是 OT 的架构性痛点，真正的代价在中心服务器和定序逻辑上。
中心定序器天生有并发上限，这本是 OT 的软肋；但这道题一开始就把编辑者摁在 100 人以内，软肋刚好被前提条件挡住了。
OT 完全支持删除，墓碑是 CRDT 的机制，不是 OT 缺失删除能力的补丁。
延迟主要来自网络距离，不是 OT 算法本身的开销，CDN 也解决不了定序问题。
optionExplanations_en: Memory footprint isn't OT's architectural pain point — the real cost sits in the central server and its ordering logic.
A central sequencer has a built-in concurrency ceiling — normally OT's soft spot — but this design caps editors at a hundred from the start, so the weakness never gets exercised.
OT handles deletes fine; tombstones are a CRDT mechanism, not a patch for something OT is missing.
Latency mostly comes from network distance, not from the OT algorithm itself, and a CDN can't fix an ordering problem.

q: CRDT 解决并发编辑的核心思路是？
q_en: What is CRDT's core idea for collaborative editing?
options: 让服务器变换每个操作
让每个操作可交换，任意顺序都收敛
禁止两个用户编辑同一段落
用时间戳做 last-writer-wins
why: CRDT 不重写操作，而是把操作设计成天然可交换：只要所有更新最终送达所有客户端，大家必然收敛一致，不需要中心定序。
why_en: CRDTs make every edit commutative so that clients converge on the same document no matter what order the operations arrive in.
options_en: Have the server transform every operation
Make every operation commutative so order doesn't matter
Forbid two users from editing the same paragraph
Use timestamps for last-writer-wins

termDefinitions.meaning: 无冲突可复制数据类型：把编辑设计成可交换操作，任意顺序应用都收敛到同一结果，无需中心服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT, or conflict-free replicated data type, makes edits commutative so replicas converge to the same result in any arrival order without a central server.

optionExplanations: 让服务器改写每个操作是 OT 的做法，不是 CRDT 的思路。
把操作设计成天然可交换，不管什么顺序应用都能收敛到同一结果，这就是 CRDT 不需要中心定序的原因。
